Implementation element FB2-SW-IMP-000001 is the code location in which the reference project's FB2-SW-DSN-000001 acquisition, PEC-validation and publication responsibilities are carried: the pinned source's LTC_Trigger sequencer, its LTC_StartVoltageMeasurement command selection, its LTC_CheckPec per-LTC integrity gate, its LTC_SaveRxToVoltageBuffer reassembly and the DMA-backed SPI transfer the design selects, which the source realises through SPI_TransmitReceiveDataDma and AFE_DmaCallback rather than through the symbols the design names. The link runs from the implementation to the design because that is the direction master prompt section 13 declares for implements (implementation element -> design/requirement).
links.reorientation_note: RE-ORIENTED 2026-10-02. This link previously read FB2-SW-DSN-000001 --implements--> FB2-SW-SWR-000001 (design on the source side, requirement on the target side) with the rationale 'Design implements software requirement'. That direction is the inverse of the one master prompt section 13 declares for implements, and the old rationale asserted the relationship rather than describing it. The link_id is unchanged so the record's identity stays traceable. Threat analysis FB2-SAF-TAR-000001 derives security requirement FB2-SAF-SEC-000001 from its threat and mitigation set; the requirement carries the mitigations forward and the TARA carries the evidence they rest on.

Authenticated and confidential transport protects the safety goal's assurance argument against a compromised or spoofed communication path.
Bounded connection admission and a per-service resource budget protect the availability leg of the safety goal's assurance argument.
CAN message integrity, freshness and length checking protect the cell-voltage functional safety requirement, whose measurement input is carried on the CAN bus.
CAN message integrity, freshness and length checking protect the SOA monitoring functional safety requirement, whose measurement input is carried on the CAN bus.
Serial-link framing, integrity and control-byte demotion protect the safety goal's assurance argument against a link that carries measurement data into the master.
Cryptographically strong entropy for network security parameters, plus governed third-party component management, feed open items that the safety-case skeleton must eventually account for.

The threat analysis supports the safety goal's assurance argument by identifying and bounding the external-interference paths to the requirements derived from that goal, and by recording the residual risk that remains unaccepted. It does not claim the goal is met.

Evidenced threat THR-005 (CAN dispatch on identifier alone, no integrity or freshness check at the shared dispatch layer) bears directly on the freedom-from-interference assumption underlying the cell-voltage requirement.
Evidenced threat THR-005 bears on the freedom-from-interference assumption underlying the SOA monitoring requirement in the same way as for the cell-voltage requirement.

Threat THR-007 is a hypothetical-project threat against a planned diagnostic and configuration write service, not a threat observed in the pinned source. The link records that the contactor-response requirement is what such a service would put at risk. No real control and no real exposure is claimed.

Threat THR-008 (engineering toolchain able to write to the target) is an open item the safety case must eventually account for; the component inventory now exists (docs/artifacts/sources/sbom.json) but the governance process around it does not.
The ASIL D limit-monitoring requirement names the debounce count and the false-positive criterion. CR-001 moves both, so the requirement is a declared target of the change request.

The hazard record expresses its degraded state in terms of the derating level, and this change rebuilds the warning/derating/shutdown ladder that defines it. The hazardous event itself does not move; the degraded-state boundary does.

The AFE accuracy requirement is stated over a 2.5 V-4.2 V measurement range. The supplier re-specification narrows the top of that range to 4.15 V, and the noise sigma derived from this accuracy is the premise of the false-positive criterion CR-001 relies on.

The SOA detailed design carries the constraint 'Debounce count configurable (default: 2)'. This change moves the default to 3, and makes the design's existing reset_debounce action load-bearing, so the design is a declared target.

The limit-monitor test embeds the ceiling in its stimulus text ('above 4200 mV limit') and the debounce count in its step count. After this change the test as written no longer exercises the behaviour it was written for, so it is a declared target rather than a regression to re-run.

The interface authority carries iso_spi_transformer_isolation_vrms = 2500 in its electrical budget. This change removes that barrier from one configuration, so the interface authority must gain a second interface and the isolation entry must be re-scoped to the retained front end only.

The AFE accuracy requirement states a device-specific error budget (+/-1.5 mV over 2.5 V-4.2 V). A second front end has a different error budget, and that budget is the premise of the noise assumption behind the SOA false-positive criterion.

All three acceptance criteria of this requirement - BER < 1E-9, failure detection within 5 ms, CRC coverage 100% - describe an isolated differential link. The migrated configuration has no such link, so the requirement must be re-derived rather than inherited.

The AFE driver software requirement is written against one device family's validation mechanism and DMA shape. Two drivers means two enforcement points for publish-before-use, so the requirement is a declared target of the change.

The driver architecture is bound to one device in an explicit part-number constraint, in a DMA buffer size that follows from that device's frame, and in an implementation mapping whose every row is an LTC path.

The plausibility stimulus bounds are the direct product of the front end's error budget and full-scale range. Its 4900 mV case sits outside any plausible cell range, so it would pass against either device while discriminating nothing - the false-green a device swap produces.

The only test exercising communication integrity injects faults into the isolated link's framing. Against a direct SPI link the same injections may not exercise the same mechanism, so a pass would be a property of the harness rather than of the design.

The ASIL D requirement specifies how many consecutive violations confirm a fault but says nothing about a partially advanced counter when the value returns in range. That silence is the root cause of the implementation divergence this change corrects.

The SOA design already specifies the DEBOUNCING -> IDLE transition with the action reset_debounce, so the design is correct and is not revised. It is a declared target of the change because the divergence was located here and the absence of a revision is a decision that belongs on the record.

The software requirement an implementation is actually written against is silent on counter reset, and its acceptance criteria are a copy of the safety requirement's. The new fail-able reset criterion must be added in both places.

The limit-monitor test performs its two violations back to back and only then an in-range sample, so it never observes a partially advanced counter at the moment of recovery. The defect is not expressible in the current step structure, which is why the measure is a declared target and not a regression to re-run.

FB2-SW-IMP-000001 realises the reference project's FB2-SW-SWR-000001 at the requirement level: acquisition is triggered through AFE_StartMeasurement into the LTC sequencer, integrity is gated by LTC_CheckPec before parsed values reach the database block, and publication is the DATA_WRITE_DATA path whose database handler stamps a header timestamp. The requirement's 20 Hz, 5 ms and 100% figures are not established by this link.

FB2-SW-IMP-000002 realises the comparison clause of the reference project's FB2-SW-SWR-000002 and, at revision 1, does not realise its debounce clause: the implementation record declares the missing per-cell debounce counter as a not_in_source proposal, so this link asserts partial realisation and says which part is missing.

FB2-SW-IMP-000003 realises the actuation and feedback-confirmation clauses of the reference project's FB2-SW-SWR-000003, with the sequencing realised one layer above in BMS_Trigger, and declares the design's cycle counter a not_in_source proposal. The requirement's 5 ms emergency-open clause is not established by this link and the configured waits the source applies are longer.

FB2-SW-IMP-000004 is the implementation element the reference project relies on for FB2-SYS-SYR-000007: the periodic BMS-state frame is the publication mechanism for the item's own mode. The link asserts partial realisation only - the requirement's limit-publication and diagnosable-refusal criteria have no code path in the pinned source and the refusal is declared as a not_in_source proposal on the implementation record.

FB2-SW-SWR-000001 is allocated to the reference project's FB2-SW-DSN-000001 as the software requirement whose implementation that design details. Direction is requirement -> design element, as master prompt section 13 declares for allocated_to.
FB2-SW-SWR-000002 is allocated to the reference project's FB2-SW-DSN-000002 as the software requirement whose implementation that design details. Direction is requirement -> design element.

FB2-SW-SWR-000003 is allocated to the reference project's FB2-SW-DSN-000003 as the software requirement whose implementation that design details. The design additionally claims sequencing and cycle counting the requirement does not state and the source does not realise; that difference is recorded on the implementation record rather than hidden by this link.

This measure is the source-grounded part of FB2-SYS-SYR-000001's verification: it decides the requirement's integrity-before-use and data-age criteria against the mechanism the pinned source defines, namely the per-LTC packet error code comparison and the database header timestamp. The link asserts those two criteria only; the requirement's acquisition-rate criterion is deliberately not covered here and is covered by FB2-VER-TMS-000022 under a different oracle kind.

This measure is the analytical part of FB2-SYS-SYR-000001's verification: it computes whether the configured acquisition period meets the requirement's rate threshold, and records the margin, which at the registry's 50 ms period is zero. It exists as a separate measure from FB2-VER-TMS-000021 so that a source-grounded pass on integrity cannot be mistaken for a pass on rate.

This measure is the source-grounded part of FB2-SYS-SYR-000002's verification: it establishes, from the nested tier comparison and the diagnosis configuration table at the pinned commit, that an excursion into the two outer tiers is graded below the safety-limit tier and cannot reach the fault reaction. It covers the requirement's degradation-discrimination criterion and not its debounce or its declared boundary.

This measure is the assumption-based part of FB2-SYS-SYR-000002's verification: it addresses the debounce and the degraded-to-fault boundary, neither of which has any counterpart in the pinned source, and it declares the assumption its outcomes rest on rather than presenting them as verified behaviour. Its paired execution record is blocked, so this link asserts that a planned verification exists and not that the requirement is met.

This measure is the analytical verification of FB2-SYS-SYR-000003: it sums the waits the pinned source's application configuration applies between the stages of opening and compares the total against the interval the requirement allocates, and it expects the comparison to fail. The link asserts that the timing claim is under verification and under contradicted, not that the requirement is satisfied.

This measure is the source-grounded verification of FB2-SYS-SYR-000004's mode-dependent reaction criterion: it establishes from the pinned source that the applicable temperature tier set is selected by the sign of the string current and that the admissibility of an initialisation request is selected by the current state. The link asserts coverage of that criterion only; the requirement's mode-publication criterion is not covered.

This measure is the only verification FB2-SYS-SYR-000005 has, and it verifies the requirement against the corpus's own declared assumption because the second-barrier element it describes does not exist in either profile. The link is deliberately weak and says so: it records that a planned verification exists against an assumption, and its paired execution record is blocked because there is nothing to execute against.

This measure is the source-grounded verification of FB2-SYS-SYR-000006's validity-marking and envelope-check criteria, established from the pinned source's current-sensor receive callback and the SOA module's gating on the invalid flag. The link asserts coverage of two of the requirement's three criteria; the third, that no invalid measurement reaches any supervisory decision, needs a consumer census this measure does not contain.
